newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon shares weak, hurt by Van der Horst.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon shares weak, hurt by Van der Horst.

text.p: Singapore noon shares stayed weak on Tuesday with poor interim results by engineering firm Van der Horst taking centrestage from Wall Street, dealers said.

"Singapore has decoupled from Wall Street a long time ago. The only possible impact on the stock market is indirect and possibly through the currency movements," a local dealer said, referring to Wall Street's 192.25 points drop on Monday.

"Today is Van der Horst's Day," another added. He said investors, shocked by Van der Horst's 84 percent plunge in net earnings for six months ended March 31, 1997, were nervous and taking a second look at other stocks once thought promising.
"The perception is a lot of companies have promised growth but might not find it easy to deliver, just like Van der Horst," the dealer said.
At 0430 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 10.77 points at 2,024.02. Turnover was light, around 50 million shares, with 75 gainers to 169 losers.

Small-capitalised stocks like Raffles Medical, Informatics and Excel Machine hit new year highs in active trade. "These firms are fundamentally all right and their share issues are small, making them easier to run," a dealer said.
